newsitem.title: DENMARK: Goldman Sachs cuts forecasts for Danish inflation.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs cuts forecasts for Danish inflation.

text.p: Investment bank Goldman Sachs has revised downward its forecasts for 1997 and 1998 Danish inflation but says the strength of economic growth still gives cause for concern regarding the longer term.

"Rising capacity utilisation and some upward pressure on wages underline the risks to the longer-term outlook and we are forecasting that consumer price inflation will average 2.1 percent in 1997 but rise to 2.7 percent (in 1998)," it said in its June/July economic analysis.
In its April survey it had forecast inflation of 2.6 percent for 1997 and 3.1 percent for 1998.
Danish consumer prices rose 1.9 percent year-on-year in May, according to National Statistics Office data.
